summary: Learn to design reliable agent teams, orchestration patterns, and observability workflows. Build practical artifacts for real AI operations.
lede: Multi-agent systems coordinate specialized AI agents to plan, delegate, and complete work through controlled workflows. This course is for professionals who design, assess, or govern AI workflows, and covers choosing orchestration patterns, structuring agent handoffs and shared memory, setting tool access rules, and reviewing traces and task evaluations to make workflows more inspectable.
audienceIntro: This course is built for professionals who need to design, assess, or govern multi-agent systems and orchestration in practical business settings. It suits people who already work with AI workflows and now need stronger architectural judgment, clearer control points, and better operational readiness.
prerequisites: Participants should have a working understanding of generative AI concepts, basic software architecture, and the role of APIs or SDKs in application workflows. Familiarity with prompt design, data handling, and simple evaluation metrics will help you move faster, but no advanced coding background is required for the conceptual and architectural exercises. If your team plans to implement agent prototypes, a laptop with access to a supported development environment and internet-enabled collaboration tools will be needed. The course is taught at the intermediate level and assumes you can already discuss AI use cases, workflow automation, and governance concerns in a business or technical setting.
